title: CLASH
scope: Kudla 2011 CLASH implementation, extracted at the level of the supplied Illumina schematic. The verified original abstract identifies a yeast RNA–RNA interaction assay; later human miRNA adaptations and related assays remain contextual. The route ends at cDNA; it does not specify a complete adapter-bearing library or a sequencing/data-analysis workflow.

method_scopes.rationale: The target is the CLASH schematic, associated with Kudla et al. 2011 by the catalogue reference, poster citation fragment and matched original abstract. It has one route: protein-associated RNA duplex A/B → UV-crosslinked complex → affinity-purified complex → end-ligated A–B RNA → cDNA. The poster repeats that route; its left CLASH emblem is a method illustration without a separate processing arrow. Neighboring miTRAP, scRNA-seq and partial other rows or chemical legends are not alternatives within this schematic. All four local actions apply at the depicted schematic level. The registered Kudla evidence is abstract only, so it does not establish omitted protein-processing chemistry or implementation-specific molecular details. Subsequent sequencing explains the informational purpose without adding a depicted measurement operation.

unknowns.question: In the Kudla 2011 implementation, how is the depicted protein-associated ligated RNA converted into the isolated RNA template for reverse transcription? The drawing retains protein and crosslink marks through ligation, while the catalogue groups RNA isolation before reverse transcription. The registered original paper is abstract only and does not describe this interface. To resolve implementation-specific protein processing or any corrected placement of that processing, acquire and register the relevant full-text workflow/Methods passage and figure from PMID 21610164 (DOI 10.1073/pnas.1017386108). This does not prevent the depicted ligation route and broad isolation/reverse-transcription block from being recorded.
